title: Preserve novel UX directions that share workflow vocabulary but change the mechanism

problem_spec.request: Propose the best UX direction for a workflow where requests move between requester, reviewer, and operator, but handoffs currently feel opaque and error-prone.
constraints: Keep the product usable on desktop and tablet.
Do not require a full navigation rewrite in the first release.
success_criteria: Make the next required action obvious without flattening the workflow into a chat feed.

candidate.thesis: Add a baton timeline that travels with each request
candidate.mechanism: Represent the handoff as a persistent baton card that shows current owner, next expected action, blocking reason, and the full state-transition timeline inside the existing request detail panel.
assumptions: Users need ownership and blocking state more than another inbox view.
strengths: Makes the current owner and next action explicit at every handoff.
failure_modes: Can become noisy if the baton state is not tightly scoped.
unknowns: How much timeline detail helps before the panel feels overloaded?
candidate.implementation_shape: Ship the baton card inside the existing detail panel on desktop and tablet first.
evidence: The brief asks for clearer handoffs without collapsing the workflow into chat.

candidate.thesis: Create a shared approval inbox with stronger next-action cues
candidate.mechanism: Keep the current workflow structure, but add an inbox-style queue that highlights urgency, owner, and next step so teams can process handoffs faster from a central view.
assumptions: A clearer queue is the main missing piece in the handoff workflow.
failure_modes: May still hide the deeper state transitions once a user opens an item.
unknowns: Will a shared queue be enough without better in-flow context?
candidate.implementation_shape: Layer an approval inbox on top of the existing navigation.
evidence: The product already has multiple actors and handoffs, so queue clarity matters.

expected_assessment.summary: Both ideas talk about handoffs and next actions, but the candidate changes the mechanism from a central queue to an in-context baton timeline attached to each request.
duplicate_signals: Shared vocabulary around handoffs, owners, and next actions.
